sections.title: Appearance
lines: A combat-trained camel in studded leather barding, usually a one-humped dromedary.

sections.title: Attacks
lines: Bite · melee · +5 to hit · reach 5 ft. · 2d4 + 3 bludgeoning

sections.title: Trait mechanics
lines: Desert Walk · Nonmagical sand that is difficult terrain costs the camel no extra movement.
Condition resistance · The block lists resistance to blinded, exhaustion.

sections.title: Bonus action mechanics
lines: Spit (Recharge 4–6) · One creature the camel sees within 15 ft. must pass a DC 13 CON save or be blinded until the end of its next turn.

sections.title: Reaction mechanics
lines: Defensive Kick · When a visible creature within 5 ft. damages the camel or its rider, that creature must pass a DC 13 STR save or be pushed up to 10 ft. away and knocked prone.

sections.title: Companion use mechanics
lines: Cost and carrying capacity · 200 gp. It can carry 480 lb.

Handler commands · A designated handler can use an action and pass a DC 10 WIS (Animal Handling) check to order it to Attack, Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Help, Hide or Use an Object. On failure the animal defends itself and otherwise takes no action.
Delivering or fetching an item · Use an Object can deliver an item. It can also fetch an item from a willing creature or one on the ground or otherwise unworn and uncarried.

Training a handler · It can learn up to four handlers, with one week of training per handler. Teaching a fifth normally replaces the handler who last commanded it least recently. At the GM’s discretion, a close bond can prevent replacement and the new training fails.
Mounted combat · While used as a mount in mounted combat, it follows the controlled mount rules.

sections.title: Table notes
lines: Black Flag fixed values are Perception 9 and Stealth 10. Ability modifiers are STR +3, DEX +0, CON +2, INT −4, WIS −1 and CHA −3. No languages or special senses.
The source also describes two-humped cavalry camels. It says trained camels protect dismounted riders.
The handling rule specifies an Animal Handling check, then calls its failure a failed save. Resolve failure using the check it specifies.
Source: Kobold Press, Player’s Guide 2 (2026), pp. 142–143.

sections.title: Appearance
lines: A small pigeon trained to carry messages in a tube fixed to its leg.

sections.title: Attacks
lines: Peck · melee · +2 to hit · reach 5 ft. · 1d4 piercing

sections.title: Trait mechanics
lines: Messenger · The pigeon knows the direction and approximate distance to up to three trained people or places on its plane. A humanoid can fasten a message tube and choose one of these destinations. The pigeon flies there directly and has resistance to exhaustion while carrying the tube.

Training · It can learn up to three humanoids or places, with a week of training for each. Teaching a fourth replaces the destination it visited least recently. It uses these destinations in place of designated handlers.

sections.title: Bonus action mechanics
lines: Resolute Delivery · It takes the Disengage or Dash action. Carrying a message tube also lets it move an extra 15 ft. before or after that action.

sections.title: Companion use mechanics
lines: Cost and carrying capacity · 8 gp. It can carry 15 lb.

sections.title: Table notes
lines: Black Flag fixed values are Perception 11 and Stealth 10. Ability modifiers are STR −4, DEX +0, CON +0, INT −4, WIS +1 and CHA −3. No languages or special senses.
The price table lists the 50-ft. flying speed. The stat block also gives a 10-ft. walking speed.
Source: Kobold Press, Player’s Guide 2 (2026), pp. 142–143.
